blocks.text: Predicate logic is an extension of propositional logic. It allows us to express more detailed statements about objects and their properties. In predicate logic, we can talk about individuals, groups, and relationships between them (as shown in Figure 2.7).

blocks.alt: A box Predicate: Helps, with arrows down to two boxes, Variable: x and Variable: y; below them, Helps (x, y).
blocks.caption: Figure 2.7: Predicate Logic Structure (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 2.7).
